full_judgment: 7. Mr. M.A. Rahim, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff respondents on the other hand has contended that the findings of fact of both the courts below as to the existence of the oral agreement contemporaneous to the pattan in 1953 by which the parties agreed the suit land to be on us factory mortgage on receipt of 200/00 taka from the mortgagee as consideration, and the possession having remained with the mortgagor with the right of reconveyance after payment of rent, the said finding of fact having been arrived at after full consideration of the evidence on record and the patta deed, they said could not be said to be a finding of fact arrived at by causing an error of law or of procedure which could be set aside by this Court. Mr. Rahim has further urged that in the presence of an oral agreement as to usufructory mortgage and subsequent reconveyance, the patta itself would not establish the real intention of the parties and that being so the oral evidence would be admissible under section 92 of the Evidence Act in order to find out from the surrounding circumstances the real intention of the parties to the contract and the nature and purpose of the contract. It would not be a case to vary the terms as such but a case of misrepresentation as contemplated under Proviso 1 and 6 to Section 92 of the Evidence Act. Hence, it is contended by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the courts below did not act illegally in admitting the oral evidence in any violation of the Provisions of Section 92 of the Evidence Act as contended.
